events.title: The Financial Side of Estate Planning: Beyond Wills and Trusts
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Most people think of estate planning as a legal task — a will, a trust, a folder in a drawer. But many of the decisions that determine how your assets actually reach your family are financial ones, made on account forms and beneficiary designations years apart. What you'll learn: What legal documents do... And don't. Wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and healthcare directives: what each one accomplishes, and where its authority stops. How your assets actually transfer. Why beneficiary designations and account titling often decide who receives what - no matter what your will says. Overlooked areas that cause issues. Outdated beneficiaries, joint ownership problems, blended families, digital footprints, overlooked retirement rules and uncoordinated advice. Taxes, family, and legacy goals. How inherited retirement accounts are taxed, and how to coordinate family, charitable, and legal decisions into a cohesive plan. Every attendee receives complimentary resources, including an Estate Planning Readiness Checklist to organize their own information. Who should attend: Retirees Those approaching retirement Parents and grandparents Anyone who has accumulated assets and wants to protect their family We are also hosting the same workshop on Thursday, October 8 at 2:00 p.m. Presented by Daniel L. Foss, Ch FC, CLU.
events.blurb: Hear a talk on the financial decisions behind estate planning, beyond just wills and trusts.

events.title: The Messenger of Peace: Japanese Crane Textile Sculpture
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Join sustainable artist and educator Leila Ghasempor for a hands-on art workshop exploring the beauty, history, and symbolism of the Japanese crane. Traditionally associated with hope, longevity, and peace. Participants will learn about the cultural meaning of the crane while exploring textile construction, sculptural form, and geometric folding techniques to create their own three-dimensional fabric crane. No sewing experience is required. All materials will be provided. This class is intended for ages 18 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Make a Japanese crane textile sculpture while learning the bird's history and symbolism with artist Leila Ghasempor.

events.title: Planning Your Cool Vegetable Garden in Our Mediterranean Climate
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Did you know that we can grow cool season vegetables in Santa Clara County? It's true! With our cool (but not cold) rainy season we can grow all sorts of vegetables like greens such as lettuce, chard and kale, to cruciferous vegetables like broccoli or cauliflower to root vegetables like beets, carrots and radishes. Come learn what you can grow with Matt Hall, UC Master Gardener. He will go over the basics such as soil, water and fertilizing requirements, and show all of the different plants that do great here. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn which cool-season vegetables grow well in Santa Clara County's Mediterranean climate.

events.title: Create a DIY Award Ribbon
events.description: Registration is required. Seats and materials are limited. Please only register if you plan on attending. Join us to create a DIY award ribbon with a personalized button in the center! You will be able to create your button from images from recycled books, magazines, and newspapers or bring in a photo of a loved one or thing. We will have a wide variety of ribbons to choose from to decorate and elevate your creation. This class is intended for adults, ages 18 and up only. events.blurb: Craft a DIY award ribbon with a personalized button made from recycled books, magazines, and newspapers.

events.title: Ukulele Jam Sing and Play Along
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Would you like to learn some fun songs on the ukulele? Beginners and ukulele enthusiasts are welcome to join us to sing and play together. Ukulele instructor Chuck Monahan will teach participants how to play basic chords on the ukulele and lead the group in an informal performance of popular songs from the last 50 years. Bring your own uke, or use one of ours. Ages 12 and up only. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Sing and strum along with ukulele instructor Chuck Monahan in a beginner-friendly play-along session.

events.title: Spirit of '76: A Look Back at Mountain View's Bicentennial
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Learn how the "Spirit of '76" excited the residents of Mountain View as they celebrated the Bicentennial. The entire year of 1976 was filled with parades, lectures, pageants, kites, fire hydrants and more. See examples of the community coming together to learn and participate in the commemoration of the Declaration of Independence. Participants will then create artwork about how they are feeling about the 250th anniversary of American independence. We'll put the artwork together to form a "quilt" in the spirit of the Bicentennial Quilt created by a group of local women in 1976. Participants will have a chance to conduct a gallery walk to observe and reflect on the other squares in our community quilt. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear how Mountain View residents celebrated the Bicentennial with parades, pageants, and kites throughout 1976.

events.title: Murder Mystery Theater
events.description: Step into the world of a mysterious mansion where one fateful evening takes a deadly turn. You'll be given a character to play, complete with secrets, suspicions, and motives of your own. As the story unfolds, clues will be revealed and everyone becomes a suspect. Work with your fellow guests to uncover hidden secrets, piece together the evidence, and determine who committed the murder before the mystery is solved. Will you crack the case, or will the murderer get away with it? No acting experience is necessary—just bring your imagination and your detective skills! Whether you're a seasoned sleuth or simply looking for a fun and theatrical evening, everyone has a role to play in this interactive murder mystery. For Grades 9-12. Registration required.
events.blurb: Take on a character role and hunt for clues as a mysterious mansion evening turns deadly.

events.title: Afghan Cassette Archive: Stories, Sounds, and Music from Afghanistan
events.description: Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Join Omid Jahan, founder of the Afghan Cassette Archive (@afghancassettearchive), for a multimedia listening session exploring Afghanistan's rich musical history through rare cassette recordings, archival materials, and personal stories. The program will highlight Afghan music from different eras and communities, including recordings preserved from Afghanistan and the Afghan diaspora. Attendees will have the opportunity to hear selections from the archive, learn about the stories behind the music and artists, and view original cassette tapes and other archival materials. The session offers a unique look at Afghan history, culture, migration, and memory through the music that has traveled across generations. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear rare cassette recordings and stories from the Afghan Cassette Archive's founder Omid Jahan.

events.title: Short Story Social: "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" by Jeanette Winterson
events.description: Love the idea of a book club but don't have time for a whole novel? Join our Short Story Social, a relaxed "book club" for short-story fans and busy readers. We meet virtually on the last Thursday of each month to discuss one or two contemporary short stories (no more than 40 pages total). Participate from anywhere—jump in late or leave early if needed! Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link. 2026 Reading List June 25th- "The Shroud" in Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq July 23rd- "Mall of America" by Suzanne Wang in The Best American Short Stories 2024 August 27th- "A Sunny Place for Shady People" in A Sunny Place for Shady People by Mariana Enriquez September 24th- "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora in The Best American Short Stories 2025. * Also available in New England Review, Vol 45, No. 2-avaialble through Gale Academic Onefile with your library card. October 29th - "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" in Night Side of the River by Jeanette Winterson
events.blurb: Discuss Jeanette Winterson's short stories "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" with fellow readers at this virtual book club.

events.title: A Taste of History: Remembering the Wine History of Mountain View
events.description: Registration is recommended. Seating is limited. Walk-ins are also welcome. Before Silicon Valley, before the apricot orchards, this region was wine country. From the first vines planted at Mission Santa Clara in 1798 to more than 100 wineries operating across Santa Clara County by the 1890s, the South Bay was once one of California's most productive wine regions. Join us for a presentation by fourth-generation Mountain View resident and museum professional Julie Bly De Vere. She will present a lively look at the winemakers, vineyards, and forgotten history that shaped our local landscape long before the tech industry arrived.
events.blurb: Hear the story of Mountain View's forgotten wine industry, from Mission Santa Clara's first vines to over 100 local wineries.

events.title: Pages and Paws
events.description: Therapy reading dogs provide a comforting presence for children as they navigate the exciting realm of books. This initiative aims to build confidence, enhance literacy skills and instill a lifelong love for reading. Therapy dogs plan to visit on the first Friday of each month, but review our calendar to confirm dates. Limited registration is intentional to allow readers rewarding one-on-one reading time with a therapy dog. More details on your confirmed time-slot, and instruction to follow once registered. Ages 8-12.
events.blurb: Read aloud to visiting therapy dogs and build reading confidence in a relaxed library session.

events.title: Sew Sew Saturday
events.description: Need a sewing machine? The Library has sewing machines (model: Baby Lock Joy) and a serger (model: Brother 1034D) that are available for use within the Library on a drop-in basis. Whether you're working on a project or need to hem a garment, this casual, welcoming space is perfect for all skill levels. Volunteers are available to answer basic sewing questions. A limited number of supplies, such as scissors and thread, are provided. You are welcome to bring your own thread if you require a particular color. No registration required -- just bring your materials and drop in! This event is intended for adults, ages 18 and up. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Drop in to use the library's sewing machines and serger for your own hemming or sewing projects.

events.title: Seed Packets Demystified
events.description: Seating is limited. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are also welcome. Do you love to look at seed catalogs and seed packets but wonder if you'd really be able to grow plants from seeds? Do you stare at the seed rack in your local nursery puzzling through what variety to plant and when you should plant it? Most seed packets contain a wealth of information to help you plant seeds of the right plant in the right place at the right time. But many of us don't bother reading the fine print, and jump straight to the planting. Join us for a lively discussion and analysis of how reading the fine print on your seed packets can help you be more successful in your garden. Infrared assistive listening systems are available for use during this event. Please see Library staff for assistance.
events.blurb: Learn how to read seed packets and catalogs so you can actually pick and grow the right varieties.

events.title: Wild Fungi of California
events.description: Join Carrie Staller from Fork in the Path for an interactive hour of hands-on fun exploring the fascinating world of mushrooms! Learn how to identify mushrooms, discover chanterelles, morels, and porcini, and understand the difference between edible and poisonous varieties. We will have some specimens to touch and smell. This program is perfect for curious minds of all ages eager to learn about the natural world. About Fork in the Path: Fork in the Path offers forest-to-ocean-to-table learning programs for the adventurous of all ages across Northern California. We believe learning to forage and eating seasonal wild food is transformational. It helps us become more connected, whole, healthy, and happy. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear Carrie Staller explain how to identify mushrooms and tell edible species from poisonous ones.

events.title: Author Talk: Banned Books Week Conversation - Stories That Shape Us
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion with Erika Lynne Jones, children's book author and illustrator of Zara in the Middle and explore how stories and images take shape, from the first spark of an idea through drafting, sketching, revision, and collaboration. We will consider why young readers deserve access to books that invite curiosity, empathy, imagination, and conversation. Erika will share insights into her artistic process, the choices behind the page, and the role children's literature can play in helping readers see themselves and better understand others. A Creativebug Program.

events.title: Cookbook Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: October's theme is "cake or pie"! Each month we have a theme that you are free to interpret however you'd like. Choose a recipe to make from one of the many cookbooks or other resources in our collection- don't worry, we'll have plenty of suggestions for you! Then we'll meet to talk about books and cooking and enjoy each other's company. Photos of your finished dish are encouraged but not required. Are you Team Cake or Team Pie? Both? This month we'll be showing our team spirit by making either a cake or a pie, depending on which team you're on. You can make it sweet or savory, big enough for a crowd or small enough to be held in your hand- it's up to you! Think a Swedish smrgstrta or a savory hand pie, or one of the many, many cupcake recipes available. Or if you really are Team Both, you might consider attempting the legendary cherpumple! Browse our incredible cookbook collection in the Library or our ebooks on Cloud Library or The Palace Project, find something that looks interesting to you, and cook! Come to our meeting ready to talk all about what you made and the book you used.
events.blurb: Cook up a dish inspired by October's "cake or pie" theme, then meet up to taste everyone's creations.

Their Halloween variety show is family-friendly fun for all ages. The show features happy ghosts, Frankenstein, the Purple People Eater, a not-so-scary spider and more…. And of course, no Halloween show would be complete without a witch! Special care is taken to make this production a kid-friendly experience.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Mountains Sing by Nguyen Phan Que Mai. Multi-generational take of the Tran family set against the backdrop of the Vietnam War. Vivid and steeped in the language and traditions of Vietnam, the book brings to life the human costs of the conflict from the point of view of the Vietnamese people themselves, while showing the true power of kindness and hope. A perfect follow up to The Women (our Nov. Selection), which brings to life the Vietnam War from an American perspective. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.
events.blurb: Discuss The Mountains Sing, a multi-generational family saga set against the Vietnam War, with fellow readers.

events.title: Informed Community Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for the Informed Community Book Club, a space dedicated to exploring and discussing pertinent social, economic, and political issues. If you are interested in participating in our democratic institutions or just making friends, join us! November's book will be The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future and What We Can Do About It, by Robert Weissman From the publisher's website: Long-time corporate accountability crusaders Robert Weissman, Public Citizen president, and Joan Claybrook, Public Citizen president emeritus, investigate how giant corporations corrupt the policy-making process to block reforms favored by overwhelming majorities of the American people, and to enrich themselves through far-reaching corporate welfare schemes. The Corporate Sabotage of America's Future And What We Can Do About It pulls back the curtain on the hidden tactics that big corporations employ to have their way in Washington, D.C. and state capitols and city halls across the nation. The discussion will be hosted by former Los Gatos Planning Commissioner and current president of the Los Gatos Anti-Racism Coalition Jeff Suzuki.
events.blurb: Discuss The Corporation and other pressing social, economic, and political issues with fellow book club members.

events.title: Sound Bath Healing Meditation
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Gaby Castro-Moroder is Back for another Sound Healing session! Come join us! Sound and music is used as a method of healing across various mediums. After being told for years that she has a healing presence, Gaby Castro started her sound healing journey and took certification courses in tuning forks, crystal sound bowls, and Tibetan sound bowls. Now she provides sound healing group and individual sessions under the name Song Pine and Stone, bringing her gentle presence to those in need. A group sound healing session runs about 60-90 minutes and includes the use of crystal sound healing bowls, Tibetan bowls, tuning forks, and various other sound healing instruments. Attendees will bring their own yoga mats, blankets, pillows, and whatever else they need to be comfortable during the session. Instruments will be played to create a sound bath and attendees will be encouraged to relax and enjoy the soft, soothing sounds. When the session ends, attendees will be asked to rehydrate and we'll discuss how the session felt for everyone. Age Range: Adults and Seniors Note: A consent form may be required and provided at the event. Attendees need to consult with their physician and get approval to attend healing sessions if they have metal in their bodies, suffered concussions, have a pacemaker, use an insulin pump, and the like. If in doubt, consult your physician before the session. The Los Gatos Library recognizes the diversity of our community and is committed to accessibility for all patrons. We strive to make every visitor feel comfortable by ensuring equal access to programs, services, and activities. If you require a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in a library program, please contact library@losgatosca.gov
events.blurb: Lie back and let Gaby Castro-Moroder's sound healing session wash over you with instruments used for relaxation.

events.title: Cookbook Swap
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Do you have cookbooks that you never use sitting around? Or are you looking to add some new books to your collection? Come to our cookbook swap and meet some fellow cookbook enthusiasts, learn about our Cookbook Club, and maybe get a new book or two while finding a new home for ones you don't use anymore. This will be our very first Cookbook Swap, and if everyone has a good time, we can look into making it a regular event. For now, we will only limit the number of books you can bring to what you can carry yourself and we ask that the books you bring are reasonably clean and in good condition. If you'd like, we'll have note cards for you to mark your favorite recipes in the books so their new owners will have a fun place to start.
events.blurb: Bring cookbooks to trade, meet fellow cooks, and pick up new titles at the swap.

events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of Milkman, by Anna Burns Winner of the Man Booker Prize. A young woman navigates romance, politics, and social judgment in Ireland during the "Troubles." The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.

events.description: Early learners (babies and toddlers) and their families are welcome to join us at the Library for Storytime, where we will wiggle, sing, read, and dance together! events.blurb: Wiggle, sing, read, and dance with your little one at this Library storytime for babies and toddlers.

events.title: Bug Power with Beetlelady! (Ages 6-12)
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Register to join in on this artistic and heroic exploration of bugs with Dr. Stephanie Dole, also known as Beetlelady! Learn all about different types of insects by interacting with live bugs, and invent your own superhero bug with a fun drawing activity! This class is for ages 6-12, and registration is required (registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event).
events.blurb: Meet live insects and invent your own bug superhero with Beetlelady in this hands-on drawing activity.

events.title: Free Repairs with Repair Café
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Do you need help repairing something? Repair Café Silicon Valley will be at the library offering free repairs on household items such as toasters, lamps, radios, clothing, bikes, and more. Limit two items per household, last repairs accepted at 2:30 PM. Visit repaircafesv.org for more information about their mission and to see when other events are scheduled.
events.blurb: Bring a broken toaster, lamp, radio, or bike and get it fixed free by Repair Café Silicon Valley volunteers.

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: Join us for a discussion of Felicia's Journey by William Trevor. A story of lost opportunities, naivety, and misplaced hopes of an Irish girl who leaves Ireland to find her boyfriend in England. By one of Ireland's most admired writers. The Monday Morning book club meets in the Library Conference Room, and new members are welcome at any time.
events.blurb: Discuss Felicia's Journey, William Trevor's story of an Irish girl chasing lost hopes in England, with the group.

events.title: Cafecito Book Club
events.address: 110 E Main St, Los Gatos, CA 95030
events.description: This book club reads exclusively Spanish books and meets on the 2nd Thursday of every month from 10-11 AM in the library's conference room (1st Floor). Este club de lectura lee libros exclusivamente en español y se reúne el segundo jueves de cada mes de 10 a 11 a. M. En la sala de conferencias de la biblioteca (primer piso).
events.blurb: Talk through a Spanish-language book with other readers in the library's first-floor conference room.

events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information Starts: August 25, 2026 Ends: December 10, 2026 Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday Time: 10:30 AM. -12:30 PM Instructor: Michelle N. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.

events.title: Live Latin Jazz with Charged Particles
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: In celebration of Banned Books Week, Charged Particles will perform Funky Latin Jazz Music with a blend of Classical Music. The Bay Area's favorite quartet playing funky Latin jazz, Charged Particles is now in its 32nd year of making music. The band features four of the country's musical virtuosos. Murray Low is a keyboard wizard with dazzling Latin-jazz technique and imaginative improvisational skills. Aaron Germain is a brilliant and innovative bass player. Along with drummer Jon Krosnick, these players are making some of the most enjoyable music in the country today. Downbeat Magazine called the band "something special" and "inventive, invigorating, and mesmerizing." Jazz Times magazine said they're "enormously talented". Nippertown Magazine said the band's performance at the Albany Riverfront Jazz Festival was "thrilling" and "the peak set of the day". The Oxford Times said their performance was "brilliant". Jazz and Blues Report said: "Charged Particles is definitely dazzling." Jazz Podium said they are "a tight unit that keeps the band sound exciting." Find out more at chargedparticles.com. Join us for an afternoon of delightful upbeat music. Location: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library, 150 E. San Fernando St., San Jose, CA 95112 - Digital Humanities Center (First Floor). Park for 90 minutes Free in the Fourth Street Garage or take public transportation.
events.blurb: Hear Charged Particles perform funky Latin jazz blended with classical music for Banned Books Week.

events.title: Mystery Book Club: All the Sinners Bleed
events.description: All adults who love to read and discuss mysteries are welcome. In October, The Plot Thickens Mystery Book Club will talk about All The Sinners Bleed by S. A Cosby. (2023) Former FBI Agent Titus Crowne ran for Sheriff in his hometown to change a bigoted local police force. He finds being the first black sheriff in a rural Virginia county no easy task. First when an active shooter at the high school kills a locally beloved high school teacher, and himself as well. Titus' continuing investigations uncover images which reveal that both the killer and his victim were connected through their participation in horrifying sexually ritual killings of seven local black children who matched the descriptions of missing persons police reports over recent years. The images also reveal an unidentified third figure who always wears a wolf mask. The Plot Thickens Mystery Book Discussions are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Hispanic/Latinx Heritage Celebrates with Mariela's Music Time!
events.description: In celebration of Hispanic/Latinx Heritage Month! No tickets, only one program! Mariela's Music Time is an educational, energetic, and interactive bilingual performance for infants, toddlers, and preschoolers and their families. It's filled with rhythms and multicultural sounds, along with the rich traditions of our Bay Area. For the past decade, Mariela has drawn upon her background in music and studies of Early Childhood Education to create a program that not only explores the music but also addresses the kids' curiosity by telling the history of the instruments and their cultures. She uses kinesthetic techniques in her bilingual storytelling to make foreign words understood. In no time, the kids are singing in another language as they dance and have fun. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.

events.description: Every now and then, libraries need a little extra love from the communities they serve. events.title: Qigong
events.description: Presenter: Amy Yang, certified Qigong instructor, International Neijin Qigong Academy. Instruction will be in English and Mandarin on Thursdays, August 6 through October 8, 2026, from 11 AM to 12:30 PM. Discover the restorative power of Qigong in this 90-minute group practice, which combines gentle movements, deep rhythmic breathing, and mindful focus to help reduce stress and increase vital energy. The exercises are simple, safe, and suitable for participants of all ages and fitness levels. Shaolin Neijin Yizhichan is a traditional Qigong system originating from the Southern Shaolin Temple in Fujian, China, with over 1,500 years of history. It is an effective practice for quickly enhancing internal energy and promoting spinal health. The method helps open the meridians, regulate qi and blood circulation, and restore balance between yin and yang, supporting overall physical and mental well-being, disease prevention, and longevity. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld. org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Pageturners: We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov ( Diary of an Invasion ) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. What will we read next? It's anyone's guess. Members suggest books, and then vote on them. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. Our reading list for 2026 follows: My Friends by Fredrik Bachman - January The Wager: A Tale of a Shipwreck, Mutiny and Murder by David Grann - February South of the Border, West of the Sun by Haruki Murakami - March Trespassers at the Golden Gate: A True Account of Love, Murder, and Madness in Gilded-Age San Francisco by Gary Krist - April The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui - May The Wedding People by Alison Espach - June Unlikely Animals: A Novel by Annie Hartnett - July Say Nothing: A True Story of Murder and Memory in Northern Ireland by Patrick Radden Keefe - August The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon - September We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida - October What We Can Know by Ian McEwan - November The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon - December. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Discuss We'll Prescribe You a Cat by Syou Ishida with fellow Pageturners book club members.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club: Latine & Hispanic Heritage Month
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Discuss a graphic novel selected for Latine and Hispanic Heritage Month with the group.

events.title: Bring Your Product Ideas to Life Using AI
events.description: Have you ever had an idea to make everyday life easier with a website, an app, or a digital tool, but didn't have the technical skills to build it yourself? Thanks to today's AI tools, you no longer need to be a coder to bring your ideas to life. You can focus on the vision while AI handles the technical details. Join presenter Viral Parekh as he walks through his own journey building mobile apps with AI, including the challenges he faced and the lessons he learned along the way. Viral is the creator of Banavu Kids Activities Finder App, available on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, designed to help parents easily find activities for kids. This session includes a hands-on portion where attendees can start bringing their own ideas to life using AI tools in real time. Target Audience Adults (but open to anyone who can use a computer independently) Prerequisites No prior experience required! All you need to bring is: A laptop. If a personal laptop is not available, participants have the option to check out a loaner laptop or Chromebook at the front desk (availability is limited). Free accounts for AI tools such as Chat GPT, Claude, Gemini, or Lovable. We recommend choosing a couple tools (since tokens are limited with free accounts) and downloading the tools before the event. About the Presenter Viral has spent over a decade working on software and hardware technologies at leading Silicon Valley companies, including Apple and Robinhood. During his career, he helped deliver world-class user experiences for products used by hundreds of millions of people every day, including Siri, Air Drop, Apple Pay, and stock trading platforms. A longtime Bay Area resident, Viral now focuses on growing his app and is passionate about giving back to the community by sharing his knowledge and experience.

events.title: Nonfiction Book Discussion: A Higher Call by Adam Makos
events.description: Book Jacket for A Higher Call Open to all adults who love to read and discuss nonfictional literature. In October, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss the dual biography, A Higher Call: an incredible true story of combat and chivalry in the war-torn skies of WWII. By Adam Makos (2013) Franz Stigler was a commercial pilot drafted into the Luftwaffe at the beginning of World War II, losing many of his friends and contemporaries to death while flying missions over North Africa, Italy and Germany. In December 1943, while on a mission over Germany, Stigler intercepted a badly damaged American B-17, commanded by Charles Brown, the other pilot covered in the biography. Rather than finish off the damaged plane, which would have meant the death of the entire B-17 crew, Stigler instead guided them toward the English Channel and back to safety. 60 years later, Brown and Stigler finally met face to face. The Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion Group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 AM in Room 201B For accessibility accommodations (ex. events.title: Cnps: talk #2 Transforming HOA Landscapes with Native Plants & Ab 1572
events.description: HOA Parking Strip landscaped with California Native Plants As California advances its water conservation goals, traditional HOA turf policies are undergoing a major shift. Starting January 1, 2029, Assembly Bill 1572 will prohibit the use of potable water for non-functional turf in HOA common areas - a mandate that will be strictly enforced. For homeowners and board members, this regulatory shift presents a powerful opportunity to replace lawn areas with native landscaping that conserves water and restores local biodiversity. In this presentation, Shelkie Tao will share why converting lawns to California native plants yields far greater long-term benefits than standard low-water alternatives. She will cover practical strategies for balancing ecological performance with polished visual appeal, selecting climate-appropriate species that thrive in structured garden settings, and effectively communicating design intent to HOA boards. Attendees will leave with actionable steps for replacing thirsty turf with vibrant, ecosystem-friendly landscapes that satisfy state mandates while enhancing neighborhood character. Speaker Bio: Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of Water Efficient Gardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs. As a sustainability-driven entrepreneur, she is committed to developing attractive, water-efficient, and ecosystem-friendly landscaping solutions. Her design work has been featured by the statewide Save Our Water campaign. Prior to founding Water Efficient Gardens, Shelkie worked for over a decade in the Silicon Valley high-tech industry. She earned a Certificate of Achievement in Environmental Horticulture and Design from Foothill College, holds an MBA from the UCLA Anderson School of Management, and is an avid trail runner who has completed 21 marathons. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Why Are Exoplanetary Systems Unlike the Solar System?
events.description: NASA's Kepler mission discovered over 4,400 transiting planets around other stars, including over 700 systems with multiple planets. This sample of exoplanet systems enables us to study planetary systems as a population, and test planet formation theory. The results are that our Solar System has a relatively rare configuration, and we don't know why. In this talk, we will explore the expectations of planet formation theory, and the constraints that are now available form observations, as we work toward the goal of understanding how common Earth-like worlds are and finding such cosmic neighbors. Speaker Daniel Jontof-Hutter is an associate professor of physics and astronomy at the University of the Pacific in Stockton. He studies planetary dynamics, what we can learn about planetary systems from their motion. His research goals include pushing the characterization of low-mass exoplanets toward the terrestrial regime, using big data and dynamical simulations. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Writers Helping Writers: From Memoir to Career Planning Book: A Journey of Discovery
events.description: How did a collection of short-story memoirs from the corporate world turn into a full-fledged career-planning book? Join author Korie Pelka for an open, interactive presentation on her wild, nonlinear path to publication. She'll pull back the curtain on how she discovered her voice, pinpointed her target reader, and clarified the impact she wanted her book to make. Expect real talk on all the foibles and missteps along the way—and how you can avoid them in your own journey. Korie Pelka holds a B.F.A. and M.A. in theater directing, which served her well during her 25-year career as a communications professional in Silicon Valley. In 2015 she left the corporate world to discover her own voice in her "third act." Today she is a certified career coach who has helped hundreds of clients navigate meaningful career transitions. Her book, Get Unstuck. Get Clear. Get Going. A Guide to Discovering the Next Stage in Your Career Journey, is a business career-planning book that provides an actionable framework for confidently navigating what's next in your life and career. Korie chronicles her third-act journey and her avid quest for the perfect gelato on her website www.koriepelka.com. California Writers Club-San Francisco Peninsula Branch members share their expertise on writing, editing, marketing, publishing and more. Writers Helping Writers resumes for their fourth year on the third Thursday of these months: October 15 January 21 March 18 May 20 Registration is not required, but if you register, you'll receive an email reminder the day before the event.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For October 18th: Topic: Desires - Natural, Necessary, and Unnecessary. Success, Ambition, Sex "One who understands the limits of the good life knows that what eliminates the pains brought on by need and what makes the whole of life perfect is easily obtained, so that there is no need for enterprises that entail the struggle for success." Principal Doctrine 21. "Great abundance is heaped up as the result of brutalizing labor, but a miserable life is the result." Fragment 73. "If there is intense striving after those physical desires that do not lead to pain if unfulfilled, this is because they arise from idle opinion; they fail to be dispelled, not because of their own nature but because of the vain fancies of humankind." Principal Doctrine 30. "Happiness and blessedness do not belong to abundance of riches or exalted position or offices or power, but to freedom from pain and gentleness of feeling and a state of mind that sets limits that are in accordance with nature." Fragment 85. "I learn from your letter that carnal disturbances make you excessively inclined to sexual intercourse. Well, so long as you do not break any laws or disturb well-established conventions or annoy any of your neighbors or wear down your body or use up your funds, you may carry out your own plans as you like. However, it is impossible not to be affected by at least one of these things. Sex never benefited any man, and it's a marvel if it hasn't injured him!" Vatican Sayings 51. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 13 (pp. 137-144) and 16 (pp. 171-179). Some Questions to Discuss: What effect do competitive relations and ambitions have on us as individuals and as a society? What does it mean to be successful for Epicurus? What would be counted as success in our society? How do we reason our understanding of success? Would we agree with Epicurus's argument on sexual desire?
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence at Rinconada Library.

events.title: Author Event: Book launch for Bruce Overby's latest novel
events.description: Join us for an evening with local writer Bruce Overby ( The Cyclone Release and recently released Tristan 4 America ) with Geri Spieler ( Housewife Assassin, Regina of Warsaw ) serving as moderator. Bruce Overby is a fiction writer with particular interest in issues of loss and belonging, family and relationships, the human condition in a technology-driven world, and addiction. His fiction has appeared in Storyglossia, the Green Mountains Review, the Evening Street Review, and the anthology Home of the Brave: Stories in Uniform from Press53. " Bookmarks," the story of a brother's struggle with alcoholism, his love of poetry, and the sometimes disturbing mix of the two, won first prize in the Lorian Hemingway Short Story Competition. Bruce's debut novel, The Cyclone Release, was a finalist in the Blue Moon Novel Competition and is available now from Madville Publishing. His second novel, Tristan 4 America, is forthcoming from Willow River Press in October 2026. Bruce is a graduate of the MFA in Writing Program at Queens University of Charlotte. A San Jose native, Bruce is a member of California Writers Club-SF Peninsula Branch and participated in Rinconada Library's inaugural book fair in April. Books will be available for purchase. Bring your questions!

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7] Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?
events.blurb: Join a friendly discussion questioning ideas about hustle, success, and independence at Rinconada Library.

Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, Transmilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at Sxsw and received critical acclaim. Trans Military was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, Side XSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to Side XSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch a documentary tracing Stasi surveillance in East Germany through Peter Keup's personal investigation into family secrets.

events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. It's evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a friendly reading and discussion group at the library tackling big questions about how we live and what we value.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard
events.description: Please join us for an informative workshop presented by UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. So you want to plant fruit trees, excellent! What kind? Are you looking for plums, apricots, peaches, apples or something less common? There are hundreds of varieties of each, how do you choose? How big should the tree be? (There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.
events.blurb: Learn from UC Master Gardeners how to choose, plan, and plant fruit trees for a home orchard.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Hear library staff break down the warning signs of holiday shopping scams before you click buy.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr, Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into my heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. H ow does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her novel A Hidden Fate about family secrets and genetic foreknowledge.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Durateion: 60 minutes

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY.), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post);"outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... Provocative.... Moving.... Beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. EP has recently moved its offices out of New York and California. The new headquarters for all operations is now in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year and currently, Bravo-the Independent Film Channel retains the rights to cablecast the film. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film but national PBS, however, has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick Mac Arthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary The Panama Deception, examining U.S. military history in Panama.

events.title: Friends of the Campbell Library Used Book Sale
events.description: Join us for the Friends of the Campbell Library used book sale! Items for sale include puzzles, games, hardback fiction books, children's books, romances, thrillers, audio books, DVDs, CDs, and a variety of 'how to' books. Pay cash, check, Zelle, card, or Venmo. Remember to bring a bag for your purchases! Sign up to hear about more upcoming Book Sales at the Friends of the Campbell Library's website: Sales - Friends of the Campbell Library

events.title: Sunday CrafterNoon

events.title: Freedom to Read: Bingo
events.description: Play bingo with banned and challenged books during Banned Books Week. Mark off squares featuring titles that have faced censorship, from classics to modern favorites. This event is part of our annual Banned Books Week celebration. Request ADA accommodations for this event.

events.title: Baby Wearing Dance
events.description: Bring your baby and a baby carrier and learn a dance to popular tunes. Expectant mothers are welcome too! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Bring your baby in a carrier and learn a dance routine set to popular tunes.

events.title: Resume Review & Interview Prepration
events.description: A well-crafted resume is vital for standing out to potential employers. Our volunteer will help you learn the essential elements of a successful resume and prepare for interviews. Gain expert tips on highlighting your accomplishments, showcasing transferable skills, and mastering the Star framework to ace your next interview. *No registration required* #sjplworkscareer
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help polishing your resume and practicing interview answers with a volunteer coach.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Native Plants for Pollinators
events.description: Check out how to work in harmony with nature by selecting California native plants that support local ecosystems, conserve resources, and provide food and shelter for pollinators, birds, and other wildlife. Master gardener Mint Pasakdee will share her experience on "Habitat Gardening" or "Backyard Restoring." Gardeners of all levels are welcome. Bring questions.
events.blurb: Hear Master Gardener Mint Pasakdee share tips for planting natives that support local pollinators and wildlife.

events.title: Knitting/Crocheting/Tatting/Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, tatting, or bobbin lace project and swap tips with fellow crafters in the community room.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.
