events.title: Homework Club
events.description: Need help with your homework or a subject in school? Students in Kindergarten through 6th grade can come to Joyce Ellington Branch Library on Wednesdays from 2 to 4 pm to get free assistance. Students can get help with their homework/school enrichment or use our Study Room as a space to work on school projects independently. Free. No registration required
events.blurb: Bring your homework for free help from tutors at Joyce Ellington Branch Library.

events.title: Freedom to Read: Your Story, Your Zine
events.description: Join us for a creative, hands-on workshop where participants design their own zines. Through art and storytelling, we explore themes of identity, self-expression, and diverse voices. All materials are provided—just bring your ideas and creativity! This event is part of our annual Banned Books Week celebration. Request ADA accommodations for this event.
events.blurb: Design your own zine exploring identity and self-expression at this Banned Books Week workshop.

events.title: Freaky Friday Night Flicks
events.description: Watch some Halloween classics at your library! Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. The library will provide popcorn, candy, and drinks. This program is for teens (ages 13-18). October 16th: Beetlejuice (1988) October 23rd: The Addams Family (1991) October 30th: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993)
events.blurb: Watch Halloween classics at the library with friends, popcorn and candy provided for teens 13-18.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteers Mike, Sally & Matt. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Hear kids read one-on-one or in small groups with volunteers Mike, Sally, and Matt at Willow Glen Library.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading, and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interactions with our librarian. Kids are also welcome to practice reading aloud. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Watch kids read one-on-one or in small groups with a librarian at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Medicare Mysteries Solved!
events.description: Are you getting ready to apply for Medicare and are confused by the different plans to choose from? Join Sandra Karol, MS, RDMS, RVT, for a monthly workshop and learn more about the different plans that will work best for you and your family. Please register directly with Sandy at isail2@earthlink.net. Attendee limit is 10 people per session.
events.blurb: Learn about Medicare plan options from Sandra Karol in this monthly workshop.

events.title: Seven Trees Overfelt Adult Education ESL Class
events.description: Free. Placement test and registration required. Learn basic reading, writing, speaking, & listening skills with your library for free! This class meets in-person at the Seven Trees Branch Library and is led by a certified English instructor in collaboration with Overfelt Adult Education Center at no cost. Call the library at (408) 808-3056
events.blurb: Build reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills with a certified ESL instructor in this free class.

events.title: Mandarin Storytime
events.description: Join us for fun stories, rhymes, fingerplays and songs in Mandarin! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and songs performed in Mandarin at this Saratoga Library storytime.

events.title: English Conversation Club
events.description: Are you looking to improve your English? Join our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club at Almaden to practice speaking. Two leaders will guide the group in weekly topics. Basic understanding of English required. The purpose of this group is to practice speaking and to increase a learner's facility and comfort in speaking.
events.blurb: Practice spoken English on weekly topics with two group leaders at Almaden's Conversation Club.

events.title: Monthly Chat with Mayor Moore
events.description: Get ready to talk about what matters most to you. Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.
events.blurb: Sit down with Mayor Kitty Moore and raise whatever's on your mind at this informal monthly chat.

events.blurb: Watch kids read to a volunteer in a small group under the Read to Children sign at Berryessa Library.

events.title: In-Person English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: The Edenvale Branch Library presents an in person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. This is a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners who want to develop and increase English Language and vocabulary skills. Participants will be practicing a variety of literacy activities. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice spoken English and build vocabulary with fellow adult learners in a welcoming conversation group.

events.title: Jewelry Making for Adults
events.description: Get crafty and relax at a jewelry-making night just for adults. Supplies will be available to create whatever you like. Make something for yourself or a gift for a friend. Better yet, bring a friend! Not sure where to start? We'll have project ideas and examples to help you get inspired. Come be creative, unwind, and have fun.
events.blurb: Adults make their own jewelry using provided supplies and project ideas at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Adaptive Activities Programming at Mount Pleasant Neighborhood Library
events.description: Join us for socializing, finding new friends and having fun with art, crafts, and games! Adaptive Activities programs are geared towards teens and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Caregivers are welcome to join. Groups larger than 10, please contact us before joining as space and seating is limited.
events.blurb: Join teens and adults with developmental disabilities for art, crafts, and games at Mt. Pleasant Library.

events.title: Crafter Dark: Halloween/Fall Keychains
events.description: This event happens on the third Wednesday of every month. This month we are making Halloween or Fall keychains or phone charms. This craft uses beads, pliers, and wire to create colorful and personalized accessories. All supplies and tools are provided by the library. There is some fine motor skill required for this craft.
events.blurb: Make Halloween or fall-themed keychains and phone charms using beads, pliers, and wire.

events.title: Everyone Can Code: Sphero Battle Robots
events.description: Use Sphero robots to compete in a balloon popping battle. Team up with students to take down your opponents. Learn the basics of Sphero. Learn to roll, aim, control the LEDs, change heading, and detect collisions. Once you have the basics down, you can practice coding through simple, beginner friendly activities.
events.blurb: Team up to pilot Sphero robots in a balloon-popping battle while learning basic coding skills.

events.title: Rose Garden Game Lounge
events.description: Come relax and have fun with our twice-monthly after-school game lounge! Enjoy a variety of Nintendo Switch games or bring your favorite games (up to T-rated) to share. Other activities and snacks provided on a rotating basis. Open to current elementary, middle, and high school students. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play Nintendo Switch games or bring your own T-rated favorites at this after-school game lounge.

events.title: Insiders: Activities
events.description: Join us for socializing, finding new friends, networking, making jokes, learn to play Dungeons & Dragons, and having fun with art! Insiders programs are geared towards teens and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Caregivers are welcome to join. Snacks will be provided. Walk-ins are welcome!
events.blurb: Socialize, make jokes, try Dungeons & Dragons, and create art with fellow teens and adults in this welcoming group.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: Jewelry Making: STEM Craft
events.description: Be a Mini Maker! Join us for a creative jewelry making craft workshop. Learn how to design and create your own unique bracelet using colorful beads and charms, and take home your very own beaded bracelet. Materials will be provided. Recommended for ages 7 and up. Perfect for beginners and experienced crafters!
events.blurb: Design and string your own beaded bracelet with charms in this STEM-themed jewelry making craft session.

events.title: Friday Fun: Legos Fun
events.description: Join us every Friday at the Willow Glen Branch Library for a fun activity for kids. Activities may include arts & crafts, special performances or workshops, and board or video games. Note: 2nd Friday of every month is free play with Legos! All supplies will be provided. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Drop in for free play with Legos and build whatever your imagination comes up with.

events.title: LEGO Fun
events.description: Join us at Tully library every Tuesday for LEGO fun. Bring your creativity and imagination to build unique models using our LEGO pieces. Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards. For children and families. No registration required.
events.blurb: Build unique models out of library LEGO pieces with your family and imagination.

events.title: LEGO Engineering Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Come join us at East Sj Carnegie Branch Library for our LEGO Club! Participate in a weekly engineering challenge or make whatever you want! Important: This event is recommended for children 5 and older. Small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards for younger children. No registration required.
events.blurb: Build and tackle a weekly LEGO engineering challenge or create your own design at this club.

events.title: Pizza and Politics
events.address: Cupertino Community Hall, 10350 Torre Ave, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Pizza and Politics is an award-winning, youth-led biannual pre-election political forum coordinated by youth for youth. The event encourages youth and teen civic engagement, makes politics more accessible, and provides young people with the opportunity to connect directly with politicians.
events.blurb: Watch teens question local politicians and dig into election issues over pizza at Community Hall.

events.title: Personal Insight Questions (PIQs) Writing Workshop
events.description: Not confident with your personal insight questions for the UC application or not sure where to start? Work one-on-one with an experienced writing instructor who will help you craft and revise your PIQs that avoid common mistakes and showcase the best of who you are to the admissions team.
events.blurb: Work one-on-one with a writing instructor to craft and revise your UC personal insight questions.

events.title: STEM Club
events.description: Drop in every Thursday afternoon for a new STEM adventure! Intended for ages 5-10, but all families are welcome. October 01 - Floating Frogs October 08 - Magic Wands October 15 - Potions October 22 - Paper Bat Challenge October 29 - Halloween Lava Lamps Free. No registration is required.
events.blurb: Drop in for a hands-on STEM activity with your kids at this week's STEM Club session.

events.title: Board Game Sunday!
events.description: Everyone is invited to play board games! Join us on the second Sunday of the month from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM. We have board games for all ages: adults, teens, and children. Come with friends & family! (The room closes at 3:30 PM, so come early enough to have time to finish your game.)
events.blurb: Sit down with friends and family to play board games for all ages at the library.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration is not required but you will receive an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Carolyn Russo
events.description: Join us for a captivating online conversation with acclaimed author and Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo as we dive into her fascinating book, The Ascent of Rauschenberg. Explore the towering legacy, unexpected inspirations, and creative heights of one of America's most influential artistic icons. Most famous for his groundbreaking "Combines"—painting and sculpture hybrids that often incorporated everyday objects—American artist Robert Rauschenberg (1925-2008) created within a range of mediums, including collage, performance, photography, and printmaking. But a connective tissue through it all was his fascination with flight. The Ascent of Rauschenberg explores the flight motif across his work, spanning birds, insects, aviation, spaceflight, sensory experiences, and metaphors for his own life. More than 150 images reveal the vibrant scope of his work, from lithographs inspired by the Apollo 11 launch that NASA invited him to witness and document, to a Combine featuring a taxidermied eagle that evokes Roman mythology. Nine accompanying essays reflect on his many flight themes and subtleties that might otherwise be overlooked. The book also includes archival photographs and personal papers from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation. About the Author: Carolyn Russo is curator of the art collection at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. She has lectured internationally on the subject of art and flight and is the author of several publications including The Ascent of Rauschenberg: Reinventing the Art of Flight, Art of the Airport Tower, In Plane View: Abstractions of Flight, and Women and Flight: Portraits of Contemporary Women Pilots.
events.blurb: Hear Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo discuss her book on Rauschenberg's creative legacy.

events.description: Now in our fourth year of partnership with Music at Kohl Mansion, we proudly present the Escher String Quartet. The Escher String Quartet has established itself as one of the most accomplished chamber ensembles of its generation. Formed in New York City in 2005, and named after the Dutch graphic artist M.C. Escher, the quartet is celebrated for performances that combine technical brilliance, interpretive insight, and a distinctive ensemble sound. The group serves as Artists of the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center and has earned international recognition for its commitment to both the core string quartet repertoire and contemporary music. The quartet has appeared at many of the world's leading concert halls and festivals, including London's Wigmore Hall, Amsterdam's Concertgebouw, the Kennedy Center, Paris's Auditorium du Louvre, and major chamber music festivals throughout North America, Europe, Australia, and Asia. Praised by critics for their precision, warmth, and expressive depth, the Escher String Quartet has received numerous honors, including the prestigious Avery Fisher Career Grant and Lincoln Center's Martin E. Segal Award. The ensemble's critically acclaimed recording projects include the complete string quartets of Alexander Zemlinsky and Felix Mendelssohn and more. Through its adventurous programming and consistently compelling performances, the Escher String Quartet continues to be recognized as one of the leading chamber ensembles on the international stage.
events.blurb: Hear the Escher String Quartet perform chamber music at Music at Kohl Mansion.

events.title: Am I Being Tracked?: A Guide to Digital Privacy
events.description: Registration is required. Every click, search, and scroll leaves a trail but how much of your life is actually being monitored, and by whom? In "Am I Being Tracked?", we take a hype-free look at the modern tracking ecosystem. First, we'll debunk some myths around online privacy. Next, we'll reframe how you think about digital privacy, shifting the goal from "total invisibility" to smart data management. Finally, you'll get a practical checklist of steps you can take right now to gain control over your personal data. About the Presenter: Iman Saleh is a local Mountain View mom and a privacy professional with more than 24 years of experience in big tech and academia. She holds a Ph D in Software Engineering and is recognized as a Fellow of Information Privacy by the International Association of Privacy Professionals (IAPP).
events.blurb: Learn how online tracking actually works and hear the myths around digital privacy debunked in this online session.

We will explore the woods and nature at night, learn about nocturnal animals' special adaptations, and test our heightened senses in the dark with games and activities. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. events.title: Online Author Talk: Cherie Dimaline
events.description: Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Métis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls. Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumor—and accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimaline's expansive literary career—from the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and Ven Co. About the Author: Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by Time magazine, one of the Best Ya Books of All Time and won the Governor General's Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel Venco debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (Aila Honor Book, Aura Award winner, Crime Writers Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor General's Award Finalist). Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Métis Community and has written and produced for Marvel, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.
events.blurb: Hear Métis author Cherie Dimaline discuss her body of work and her novel Funeral Songs for Dying Girls.

events.title: Teen Halloween Roller Derby!
events.description: Join the Library for an afternoon of skating and crafting for teens at the Mitchell Park Bowl! This event will include free skating and equipment (roller skates, safety equipment) if needed, food, and a chance to win raffles prizes! Our program includes: Two skating sessions from 2-3:30 PM and 3:30-5 PM with Open Skate Spaces Free pizza and snacks throughout the three hour event, with Mister Softee Ice Cream from 2:30-4:30! Crafts Raffle prizes! A few things to keep in mind: When registering, please enter the attendee's name All attendees must fill out this waiver to skate with us! Costumes are welcome and encouraged, however please consider comfort and safety for roller skating Many thanks to the Community Services Department and the Friends of the Palo Alto Library for their support of this program and overall teen mental health and wellness in our community.
events.blurb: Skate and craft with fellow teens at Mitchell Park Bowl, with equipment and food on hand.

events.title: Halloween Storytime & Trick-or-Treat Parade (Ages 0-5)
events.description: Join us for a not-so-spooky Halloween celebration at the Library! Costumes are not required but encouraged at this Halloween-themed Storytime, which will take place outdoors on Civic Center Lawn. The fun continues afterwards in our Trick-or-Treat Parade, where we will circle around the Civic Center fountain. Library staff, Town staff, our friends from the New Museum of Los Gatos, LGS Recreation and the Friends Bookstore will have some goodies to pass out. Bring a bag or bucket for collecting goodies as you practice saying "trick or treat" (in words or in smiles!) See you there at the cutest event of the year!
events.blurb: Join an outdoor Halloween storytime on Civic Center Lawn, then march in the trick-or-treat parade.

events.title: Online Author Talk: E. Lockhart
events.description: Join us for an exciting author talk with #1 New York Times bestselling author E. Lockhart as we reflect on her impressive body of work, including the literary sensation We Were Liars, and even gain an exclusive sneak peek into her shimmering new thriller, The Pools. Once, in a small New England town known for its hot springs, something terrible happened. Something that should have been a warning to stay away from the pools, if the stories were to be believed. But no one is afraid of the water anymore, even if they should be. When new girl Lexie meets golden boy Chester, their chemistry is undeniable. She's running from a glittering life she won't speak about. He's hiding secrets of his own. Their connection feels bigger than both of them, despite their damage. One frigid winter morning in that small New England town, five people go for a swim in the pools. Five people, including Chester. What happens there sends shock waves through the town, changing life as Lexie knows it forever. Lockhart and ask questions live! About the Author: Lockhart is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the Liars novels: We Were Liars, Family of Liars, and We Fell Apart. We Were Liars is also an original series on Prime Video. Her other books include Again Again, Genuine Fraud, and The Disreputable History of Frankie Landau-Banks. She has been a finalist for the Los Angeles Times Book Prize and the National Book Award and an honoree for the Printz Award. She lives in Brooklyn, New York.
events.blurb: Hear E. Lockhart discuss We Were Liars and get a preview of her new thriller, The Pools.

events.title: FOPAL Book Sale
events.description: Don't miss this month's Friends of the Palo Alto Library Book Sale! There will be three rooms with over 70,000 books, CDs, DVDs, puzzles, etc., new & gently used, all sorted, very reasonably priced! Proceeds benefit the Palo Alto libraries. For the safety and comfort of all participants, masks are suggested and room occupancy will be lower than usual. Please visit fopal.org for more information. Saturday Hours: Bargain Room 9:30 AM – 4 PM Children's Room 10 AM – 4 PM Main Room 11 AM – 4 PM Sunday Hours: All Rooms 1 PM – 4 PM
events.blurb: Browse three rooms of used books, CDs, DVDs, and puzzles at the Friends of the Palo Alto Library sale.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Paul Vigna
events.description: Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin, in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier, Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today's global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today's secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. Through engaging anecdotes, original research, and fresh perspectives on the causes of the many challenges we face today, Vigna makes a compelling argument that money has no power apart from the power we give it. Whether you are interested in economic history, personal finance, or the hidden cultural forces shaping modern life, this talk is sure to pique your interest. About the Author: Paul Vigna is an author, journalist, editor and speaker, with a particular focus on capital markets and cryptocurrencies. He is the author of Guts: The Anatomy of The Walking Dead and coauthor of The Age of Cryptocurrency and The Truth Machine. For 25 years, he was a reporter and editor for Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal, pioneering coverage of the cryptocurrency sector. He has appeared on CNN, Cnbc, Msnbc, Fox, and PBS.
events.blurb: Hear journalist Paul Vigna discuss how money evolved into a stand-in for morality and virtue.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Pyet Despain
events.description: Prepare your palate for a vibrant culinary journey with star chef Pyet De Spain, the inaugural winner of Gordon Ramsay's hit television competition Next Level Chef, as she presents her debut cookbook, Rooted in Fire: A Celebration of Native American and Mexican Cooking. Pyet De Spain rose to prominence as the first winner of Gordon Ramsey's Fox television show Next Level Chef. Now, in her debut cookbook, she shares the joy of cooking fueled by her burning passion for Native American and Mexican American cuisine. Pyet shows you how to incorporate a delicious range of key ingredients—from venison, dandelion greens, to sunchokes, bison, and native berries—into more than sixty fusion dishes. Family and friends will be excited to gather around the table to enjoy sweet and savory food such as: Three Sisters Salad Bison and Sweet Corn Soup Fry Bread Mexican Chocolate & Mezcal Cake Corn Silk and Honey Tea Wojapi BBQ Sauce Rooted in Fire is far more than just a collection of recipes; it is a movement giving voice to Indigenous culture, histories, and foodways through the universal language of food. Register for this event today and learn how to work with nature in your own kitchen. About the Author: Pyet—short for her inherited Native American name, Pyetwetmokwe—is a member of the Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation and an award-winning global private chef. She made history as the first winner of Gordon Ramsay's Next Level Chef and was named one of Entrepreneur Magazine's Top 25 Private Chefs in Los Angeles. Her work is centered on uplifting Indigenous foodways within the culinary industry while advocating for a more sustainable and sovereign food system for Indigenous peoples.
events.blurb: Hear chef Pyet De Spain talk through her debut cookbook of Native American and Mexican recipes.

events.title: Online Author Talk: Rebecca Roanhorse
events.description: Step into a sprawling world of celestial magic, political intrigue, and ancient prophecies with New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Roanhorse as we dive deep into her acclaimed Between Earth and Sky trilogy. Black Sun, Fevered Star, and Mirrored Heavens are inspired by the rich and diverse cultures of the pre-Columbian Americas, reshaping modern speculative fiction with unmissable worldbuilding. Black Sun, the first book in the trilogy, introduces us to the holy city of Tova. The winter solstice is usually a time for celebration and renewal, but this year it coincides with a solar eclipse, a rare celestial event proscribed by the Sun Priest as an unbalancing of the world. Meanwhile, a ship launches from a distant city bound for Tova and set to arrive on the solstice. The captain of the ship, Xiala, is a disgraced Teek whose song can calm the waters around her as easily as it can warp a man's mind. Her ship carries one passenger. Described as harmless, the passenger, Serapio, is a young man, blind, scarred, and cloaked in destiny. As Xiala well knows, when a man is described as harmless, he usually ends up being a villain. Whether you are a longtime fan of the trilogy or searching for your next immersive fantasy read, this is an event you won't want to miss out on. About the Author: Rebecca Roanhorse is a New York Times bestselling and Nebula, Hugo, and Locus Award-winning speculative fiction writer. She has published multiple award-winning short stories and novels, including two novels in The Sixth World series, Star Wars: Resistance Reborn, Race to the Sun for the Rick Riordan imprint, and the Hugo Award-winning epic fantasy trilogy Between Earth and Sky. She was the guest editor of America's Best Science Fiction and Fantasy (2023) and a contributor to the New York Times "100 Best Books of the 21st Century." She has also written for Marvel comics and games, and her TV writing includes FX's A Murder at the End of the World, and the Marvel series Echo for Disney+. She has had her own work optioned by Paramount, Amazon Studios, Netflix, and AMC Studios.
events.blurb: Discuss Rebecca Roanhorse's Between Earth and Sky trilogy with the New York Times bestselling author.

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!) Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard) Crafts (in Adobe Room) All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Get henna, try rangoli chalk art, and join other activities celebrating Diwali at Mitchell Park Community Center.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. No partner needed and beginners welcome! You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you will get an email reminder for the program including a link to the class playlist to practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps with Sandy and Kent to international music, no partner or experience needed.

events.title: Deer Hollow Spooky Storytime
events.description: Together with our friends at Deer Hollow Farm, our librarians will present a spooky-themed storytime at the farm with books, songs, and rhymes. We will also get to meet some of the farm animals up close! Meet us there: Deer Hollow Farm, 22500 Cristo Rey Dr., Cupertino Please note: the parking lot for Deer Hollow Farm is about a one-mile flat, paved walk to the farm. We recommend walking shoes, hats, and/or strollers. Also, there will be limited seating-- prepare to sit on the floor if you can.

events.blurb: Hear a spooky-themed storytime with books, songs, and rhymes, then meet farm animals up close.

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk along Stevens Creek with a naturalist to learn about the Steelhead life cycle and riparian habitat.

events.title: Demons, Creatures and Monsters - Oh My!
events.description: Registration is required. Meet the mythical creatures, legendary beasts, and terrifying monsters that have populated Asian art for centuries. Appearing throughout folklore, stories, songs, and works of art, these supernatural, mystical, and often godlike (or demonic) beings have fascinated audiences since ancient times. Presented by the Asian Art Museum. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Hear about the demons, creatures, and legendary beasts that populate centuries of Asian art and folklore.

events.title: Drop-in Bike Clinic
events.venue: Bike Fix-it Station (Outside Franklin St. Entrance)
events.description: Come join us every third Saturday of the month for the Drop-in Bike Clinic! Use our tools to work on your bike. All ages welcome. Professional bike mechanic Ryan Murphy will be available for advice and help with: Changing a tire Adjusting gears and brakes Identifying that mysterious noise, and more! Meet at our Dero Fix-it station, on Franklin Street. This event is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Mountain View Library.
events.blurb: Bring your bike and use the tools on hand while mechanic Ryan Murphy offers repair advice.

events.title: NUMU Youth Still Life: Spooky Skeleton Figure Drawing (Ages 7-16)
events.description: Meet us at the New Museum Los Gatos, where the staff will arrange a (fake decor) skeleton and a (decor) dog skeleton along with a few spooky objects from our collection for children ages 7-16 to sketch on black or gray paper with white drawing pencils. This event is a young artist's dream as it will take place in the Museum's professional studio setting! All materials are provided. Registration opens 3 weeks prior to the event.
events.blurb: Sketch a decorated skeleton and spooky museum objects in white pencil on dark paper at NUMU.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shoulder Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the trails with a Park Ranger to spot and identify local birds like hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.

This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.
